$comment: Charles HTTP debugging proxy 5.1 TLS fingerprint — verified against a real Wireshark capture of Charles forwarding traffic to tls.browserleaks.com. Charles is written in Java, so the wire format reflects the JDK 11+ SSLEngine defaults: TLS 1.2 only (no TLS 1.3 cipher suites, no TLS 1.1 either), no GREASE, no ALPS, no compress_certificate, full Java signature_algorithms list (RSA-PSS / ECDSA / RSA-PKCS1 / legacy DSA), signature_algorithms_cert (ext 50) and status_request_v2 (ext 17) with fixed raw payloads. legacy_session_id is empty (length 0) on fresh connections — Java SSLEngine does NOT send a 32-byte session_id placeholder unlike browsers. Extension order: SNI → status_request → supported_groups → ec_point_formats → sigalgs → sigalgs_cert → alpn → status_request_v2 → extended_master_secret → supported_versions → renegotiation_info. When Charles is used as a MITM, the H2 frames it forwards to the origin still look like the original browser (Chrome here, akamai hash 52d84b11737d980aef856699f885ca86) — the H2 fingerprint does NOT belong in this TlsProfile and is recorded separately.
name: Charles 5.1

extensions._comment: server_name (SNI) — Java SSLEngine emits SNI first, verified by Wireshark capture
signature_algorithms_cert (Java explicitly emits this; payload is the same 19-entry list as ext 13, length 0x0026 = 38 bytes)
status_request_v2 (Java/JDK only; list len 7, OCSP-MULTI type 2, responder_id_list/extensions all empty)
supported_versions (Java still sends this even when capped at TLS 1.2)
